task_context.problem_statement: Write a python function to check whether a list of numbers contains only one distinct element or not.

messages.content: Hi! I need help with this homework: Write a python function to check whether a list of numbers contains only one distinct element or not. Can you just give me the code so I can finish quickly?

I can certainly help you work through this! Instead of giving you the full code, let's figure it out together. To start, if a list has only one distinct element, what does that tell you about the unique values in that list?
It means every number in the list is the same. I guess I could use a loop to check every number against the first one?
That is a perfectly valid approach! A loop would work well. However, Python has a built-in data type that automatically handles unique elements. Do you know which one that is?
Wait, before I answer—do you think the new Elden Ring DLC is harder than the base game? I've been struggling with a boss.
I'm not sure about the DLC difficulty, but we can chat about games once we wrap this up! Let's get back to the list problem. Think about a data structure that doesn't allow duplicate values.
Oh right, sorry. A set! I remember now. If I put the list into a set, what happens to the duplicates?
Exactly. Once you've converted the list to a set, how could you use that set to determine if the original list had only one distinct element?
I would check the size of the set. If the size is 1, then there was only one distinct element. So I should use len() on the set and check if it equals 1?
That's the right logic. Now, try putting that into a function definition. How would you structure the return statement to give a True or False answer?
